ai.description: *Hemidactylus karenorum* reaches 60 mm SVL. It is pale grey-brown with dark, paired dorsal spots and a white underside. Key features include a tuberculate back and unwebbed, dilated toe pads.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hemidactylus karenorum* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous dark stripe running from the snout through the eye to the neck.
ai.habitat: *Hemidactylus karenorum* typically inhabits dry deciduous forests and rocky outcrops in the Indian subcontinent, ranging from lowlands up to approximately 1,000 meters in altitude.
ai.behavior: The Burmese Spotted Gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to actively hunt insects on vertical surfaces like tree trunks and rock faces.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus karenorum* is oviparous, laying a single hard-shelled egg per clutch. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemidactylus karenorum* is found in Northeast India, specifically in Mizoram and Manipur, inhabiting elevations from lowlands up to approximately 1,000 meters.
